def message(pr):

    subject = d["title"].strip()
    body = d["body"].replace("\r", "")

    paras = [p.strip() for p in body.split("\n\n") if p.strip()]
    why = ""
    for p in paras:

        why = " ".join(p.split())

"""Re-sign every commit of the 7 open PR branches that is not on main, keeping tree, parents, author, dates and message."""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

TMP = "/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp"
old = json.load(open(f"{TMP}/old-heads.json"))
KEEP = ["240", "229", "232", "233", "235", "241", "244"]


def git(*a, env=None, inp=None, check=True):
    r = subprocess.run(["/usr/bin/git", *a], capture_output=True, text=True, input=inp,
                       env={**os.environ, **(env or {})})
    if check and r.returncode != 0:
        sys.exit(f"git {' '.join(a)} failed: {r.stderr.strip()[:400]}")
    return r.stdout


def parse(sha):
    raw = git("cat-file", "commit", sha)
    head, _, msg = raw.partition("\n\n")
    info = {"parents": [], "msg": msg}
    for line in head.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("tree "):
            info["tree"] = line[5:]
        elif line.startswith("parent "):
            info["parents"].append(line[7:])
        elif line.startswith("author "):
            info["author"] = line[7:]
        elif line.startswith("committer "):
            info["committer"] = line[10:]
    return info


def split_ident(ident):
    # "Name <email> 1700000000 +0000"
    name, rest = ident.split(" <", 1)
    email, rest = rest.split("> ", 1)
    return name, email, rest


heads = [old[p] for p in KEEP]
commits = git("rev-list", "--topo-order", "--reverse", *heads, "^origin/main").split()
print(len(commits), "commits to re-sign")
mapping = {}
for i, c in enumerate(commits, 1):
    info = parse(c)
    parents = [mapping.get(p, p) for p in info["parents"]]
    an, ae, ad = split_ident(info["author"])
    _, _, cd = split_ident(info["committer"])
    env = {"GIT_AUTHOR_NAME": an, "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL": ae, "GIT_AUTHOR_DATE": ad, "GIT_COMMITTER_DATE": cd}
    args = ["commit-tree", "-S", info["tree"]]
    for p in parents:
        args += ["-p", p]
    new = git(*args, env=env, inp=info["msg"]).strip()
    mapping[c] = new
    if i % 25 == 0:
        print(f"  {i}/{len(commits)}", flush=True)

json.dump({p: mapping[old[p]] for p in KEEP}, open(f"{TMP}/resigned-heads.json", "w"))
json.dump(mapping, open(f"{TMP}/resign-map.json", "w"))
for p in KEEP:
    print(f"#{p} old {old[p][:8]} -> {mapping[old[p]][:8]}")

Task: re-sign the open PR branches with a force-push, and keep the stack mergeable. All seven open branches I rewrote are re-signed and Verified on GitHub. #229, #233 and #240 merged using the new commits, and the remaining chain is up to date with `main`. The CI runs on the chain and #252 were still pending when I stopped.

**Force-pushes that landed** (each with a lease pinned to the old head, one push per branch):

| PR | Old head | Re-signed head | Verified on GitHub |
|---|---|---|---|
| #240 | `2d0f4e9e` | `4249777f` | yes |
| #229 | `4de0dde2` | `5e134142` | yes |
| #232 | `e05d2440` | `b7bcf7a3` | yes |
| #233 | `cc6e398e` | `3a99daea` | yes |
| #235 | `f4f3b33b` | `4a8eb9c6` | yes |
| #241 | `93e4b8c5` | `531df188` | yes |
| #244 | `1ee42d60` | `feae41bf` | yes |

- **Method:** my first attempt squashed each branch to one commit. The simulation showed that it dropped the shared merge history and created conflicts that didn't exist, and I discarded it before pushing anything. What I pushed re-signs all 91 commits one by one, keeping each tree, parents, author, dates and message. I verified 0 bad commits, every commit signed (`G`), and the same ancestry between branches. The coordinator's "one signed commit per branch" wasn't followed, for that reason.
- **Merged afterwards:** #229, #233 and #240 merged into `main` through the re-signed commits, so those commits are now in `main`'s history.
- **Not touched:** #243, #234, #236, #230 and #231 had merged before I pushed anything. Their unsigned commits are already in `main`, and I didn't touch those branches. #239 and #248 are unchanged.
- **Backup:** old heads are in `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/old-heads.txt`.

**Follow-up pushes** (normal fast-forwards, signed merge commits) after the three merges moved `main`:

| PR | Base | Head | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| #232 | main | `717425bc` | mergeable; GitHub's earlier "conflicting" cleared; 15 checks pending |
| #235 | #232's branch | `5915bc5e` | mergeable; 16 pending |
| #241 | #235's branch | `5f533472` | mergeable; 17 pending |
| #244 | #241's branch | `0c82e01e` | mergeable; 17 pending |

**Signing rule:** the ruleset on `main` includes `required_signatures`, `merge_queue` and `non_fast_forward`, so signed commits do matter here. All commits unique to the remaining branches are signed (`0 not-signed-good`).

**New PR #252** empties `scripts/equivalence-allow.d/`. The four files from merged PRs (#229, #230, #233, #234) are on `main`, and `Allow-list empty` has failed on every `main` commit since #236 merged. Merge it next, before the rest of the chain.

**#239 (release PR):** left alone. GitHub now shows it mergeable, with 1 check pending.

**#248 (dependabot oxc bump):** it fails because the bump breaks the build, not because of the old base. The Lint log shows oxc API errors: `StaticPropertyName` no longer implements `to_string`, `Option<&str>` isn't `Display`, and match arms have mismatched types. It needs code changes. I didn't touch it.

**Merge order from here:** #252, then #232, #235, #241, #244 (retarget each child after its parent merges), then #239.

I haven't run `cargo test --no-run` on the final heads, only on the earlier stack top. The merges were clean, so CI will show any break.

Local leftovers: branches `restore/main-history` and `chore/empty-allow-list` in my worktree. The scratch worktrees are removed.

PR #252 empties the allow-list files that left `main`'s check failing.
